info.title: Tuma API
info.description: Backend API for the Tuma commerce + delivery platform

delete.summary:
Hard-delete a customer account. The profile, refresh tokens, and order
history follow via ON DELETE CASCADE — permanent, and the platform
confirms before calling. Scoped to customer accounts: any other identity
is a 404.

404.description: No customer with that id
No customer with that id

201.description: Merchant business created with its owner account

200.description: The business, its stores, and its members

404.description: No merchant business with that id

delete.summary:
Hard-delete a business. Its memberships, stores (and their assortments),
and catalog products follow via ON DELETE CASCADE. Member ACCOUNTS are
identities, not parts of the business — they survive the delete.

404.description: No merchant business with that id
No merchant business with that id

201.description: Rider created with its OTP account and unique rider number

delete.summary:
Hard-delete a rider's account (the profile cascades) — the remedy for a
typo'd phone at creation. Blocked with a typed 409 when any delivery
ever referenced the rider: assignment history is operationally real,
deactivation is the tool for a rider who stops riding.

404.description: No rider with that id

409.description: Rider has delivery history — deactivate instead

404.description: No rider with that id

get.summary: Platform-wide counts for the admin dashboard.

post.summary:
Platform sign-in (merchant operators and admins) with email + password.
Sets the two session cookies (15-min access JWT + 30-day opaque refresh);
the body is empty. Authorization is resolved from profiles — an account
with neither an admin profile nor a merchant membership cannot enter the
platform, and the answer never reveals which part failed.

401.description: One generic error for every failure path

200.description: Always the same response — reveals nothing about the phone number
Code valid — account and customer profile fetched or created, token issued

post.summary:
Change the caller's own password. Merchant operators and admins only in
practice — customers have no password (OTP accounts), which is a 400.

401.description: Not authenticated, or current password is wrong

get.summary:
The rider's active work list — one card per delivery still out for
delivery: the store to collect from, the destination, and the customer
to call when close (the Kigali protocol — the data already flows).

200.description: This rider's deliveries that are out for delivery, newest handoff first

post.summary:
The rider's Delivered action: food handed over + cash received, one
real event. Advances the store order and settles that delivery's
payment allocation (the group's payment becomes collected when every
allocation is settled — the tracking doc's cash state).

400.description: The delivery is not in a deliverable state

404.description: Not one of this rider's deliveries

post.summary:
The rider's phone checking in (~every 5s while delivering). The
≥25m/15s GPS-noise rule lives in the domain — a throttled push answers
the same 204 as a recorded one, so the client cannot tell and need not
care.

204.description: Position accepted (recorded or throttled — same answer)

404.description: Not one of this rider's deliveries

409.description: The delivery is not out for delivery

404.description: No object at that key

200.description: The authenticated account with its profiles and memberships

patch.summary:
Updates the caller's own profile name — the customer profile when there
is one, else the admin profile. Merchant-operator accounts have no
editable name in V1 (their identity on the wing is the business).

400.description: Empty name, or no editable profile

200.description: Incoming store orders across authorized stores, newest first

403.description: No merchant membership, or not the business owner

delete.summary:
Delete a catalog product. Every store selling it loses it at once
(ON DELETE CASCADE) — permanent, and the platform confirms first.

403.description: No merchant membership, or not the business owner

404.description: Not one of this business's products

403.description: No merchant membership, or not the business owner

404.description: Not one of this business's products
Not one of this owner's products

403.description: Only the business owner manages the catalog

404.description: Not one of this owner's products

415.description: Not a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image

delete.summary:
Resolve nothing here — each handler fetches its own image through
`product_for_merchant` (ownership) + `product_image_by_id` filtered on
the product id, so a foreign product, a foreign image, or a mismatched
pair is the same 404.

403.description: Only the business owner manages the catalog

404.description: Not one of this owner's images

204.description: The image is now the cover

403.description: Only the business owner manages the catalog

404.description: Not one of this owner's images

get.summary:
One store order's detail — the fulfillment sheet: what to prepare, where
it goes, and who to call. Store-scoped managers may read only their own
store's orders; a foreign one is a plain 404.

200.description: The store order's detail with items and the customer contact

404.description: Not one of this operator's orders
Not one of this operator's orders

400.description: The order is not in a handable state (preparing, or re-assign while picked_up)

404.description: Not one of this operator's orders, or no active rider with that number

200.description: The assortment across reachable stores, oldest first

201.description: Product attached to the store's assortment

403.description: No merchant membership, or store out of scope

404.description: Unknown store or product (or another business's)

409.description: This store already sells this product

delete.summary:
Detach one product from one store. The catalog identity stays — the
product can be attached (differently priced) somewhere else.

403.description: No merchant membership, or store out of scope

404.description: Not one of this business's store products

403.description: No merchant membership, or store out of scope

404.description: Not one of this business's store products

200.description: The stores this operator can reach, oldest first

403.description: No merchant membership, or not the business owner

404.description: Not one of this operator's stores

delete.summary:
Hard-delete one of the operator's stores. Its store_products follow via
ON DELETE CASCADE — permanent, and the platform confirms before calling.
Owners only: a store-scoped manager cannot delete their store.

403.description: No merchant membership, or not the business owner

404.description: Not one of this operator's stores
Not one of this operator's stores

201.description: Banner stored; the store's image_url now serves it

404.description: Not one of this operator's stores

415.description: Not a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image

404.description: Not one of this operator's stores

get.summary:
Serves the OpenAPI contract. This is the single source of truth for
clients: the platform generates its API client from it (see
tuma-docs/Tuma_API_Architecture.md), the mobile client is written
against it by hand.

200.description: OpenAPI contract for the Tuma API
Already placed — the retry's idempotency key matched an existing group

201.description: Checkout placed — one group with its store orders

409.description: Store closed, item unavailable, or not enough stock — details name the offenders

200.description: One order group with its store orders and payment

404.description: Group not found (or not yours)

400.description: The order can no longer be cancelled (already out)

404.description: Not one of your orders

get.summary:
The customer's tracking snapshot for one order group: one delivery
entry per store order (each its own story), the real last positions,
the cached route, the ETA target, and the freshness marker the next
poll echoes back as `since`. 204 when nothing changed since.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC-3339 timestamp; 204 when the group has nothing newer

404.description: Another customer's order — indistinguishable from a missing one

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term matched against product names (stores section: name + category); empty = popular products + all open stores

200.description: Discovery: products and stores sections, both honoring the search term and the open-store rule

400.description: Only one of lat/lng, a coordinate out of range / not a number, or a search term over 100 characters

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term matched against store name and category; empty = no filter

200.description: Open stores, oldest first — or nearest first when the request carries a location (coordinate-less stores trail); filtered to name/category matches when q is present

400.description: Only one of lat/lng, a coordinate out of range / not a number, or a search term over 100 characters

404.description: No open store with that id

AdminStoreResponse.description:
A store inside the admin's business detail — standing facts plus how
many store products it sells. No location or image until something
displays them.

reason.description:
Optional client explanation — recorded in a later slice when the
cancellation event log lands; accepted now so the UI can send it.

idempotency_key.description:
A client-generated key: retrying the same checkout with the same key
returns the group it already created instead of placing twice.

items.description: At least one line. Each carries the store_product id and quantity.

CreateMerchantInput.description:
Provision a merchant business: the business row, the owner's account
(email + password, hashed by the AccountManager), and the owner
membership — one transaction. The owner signs into the merchant wing
with that account; the business itself never logs in.

CreateRiderInput.description:
Create a Tuma rider: an OTP account (phone only — the rider signs in
with the exact customer flow) plus the rider profile with its unique
rider number, in one transaction. The number is generated server-side;
the merchant will ask the rider for it at handoff.

category.description: What the store sells, in one word or two (e.g. "Grill", "Bakery").

price.description: Integer RWF, the store's own price for this product.

stock.description:
`null` (or absent) = untracked. A number is the on-hand count the
checkout reserves.

store_id.description: Which of the operator's stores sells it.

CustomerAdminResponse.description:
A customer account on the admin's list: the profile (name) joined with
the account facts (phone, active flag).

eta_target.description: Server-provided target the client decays against.

route_polyline.description:
The road route cached at handoff, or null when no routing backend
is configured — never invented geometry.

store_contact_phone.description: The overdue customer's "call the store" action (D5 surfaces it).

store_order_id.description:
The per-store card key — the client joins it to the group detail's
store orders.

trail.description: The recent real positions (tail), oldest first.

stores.description: Which stores are fulfilling this purchase.

HandoffInput.description:
The fulfillment sheet's "Handed to rider" action (tracking doc §5): the
merchant types the rider's unique number, the server validates an
active rider, assigns the delivery, and advances the order to
`picked_up`. Runs again while the delivery isn't delivered (the
wrong-number remedy); after `delivered` the assignment is frozen.
Foreign store orders are a plain 404, like every merchant route.

rider_number.description:
The rider number the store asked for — the whole assignment
interface; there is no directory picker.

ImageUpload.description:
The multipart schema in the OpenAPI contract — hey-api generates a
FormData request type from it.

file.description: The image file (JPEG, PNG, or WebP; at most 5 MB).

MeResponse.description:
The authenticated account with its authorization context. Deliberately
not the raw domain rows — responses never carry `password_hash`. The
account itself is roleless; what it can do is visible in the profiles
and memberships below, all resolved fresh per request.

oneOf.description:
The rider profile — present only on rider accounts. A rider has no
customer profile; rider mode is their surface.

store_id.description:
`null` = the whole business; a value = this member is scoped to that
one store.

MenuItemResponse.description: One item of a store's menu, as the customer sees it.

images.description:
The full gallery, cover first (composed URLs). Empty when the
product has no uploads.

MerchantOrderItemResponse.description: One frozen line, with the line total the customer saw.

MerchantResponse.description: A merchant business as the admin sees it.

MerchantStoreOrderDetailResponse.description:
The full store-order detail for the operator: what to prepare (items),
where it goes (address + coordinates), who to contact (customer name +
phone), and the money. This is the fulfillment sheet.

MerchantStoreOrderResponse.description:
A store order on the merchant's board: what to fulfill, for whom, and
where.

OrderGroupResponse.description:
The customer-facing purchase: one checkout, N store orders, one
payment. `status` is derived from the children server-side.

OrderItemResponse.description: One frozen line of a store order.

ProductHitResponse.description:
One product hit as the API returns it: the store_product (what the
customer buys, per-store price) dressed by its catalog identity and
the open store that fulfills it. Distance facts ride along exactly
like the store feed's — server-computed, never client math.

ProductImageResponse.description: One gallery image as the API returns it.

image_url.description:
The URL the object is served from (composed against the
environment's public storage base).

ProductResponse.description: A catalog product as the API returns it.

RiderAdminResponse.description: A rider as the admin sees them.

is_active.description: `false` = not assignable at handoff (the rider can still sign in).

RiderProfileResponse.description:
The rider profile as the account itself sees it: identity plus the
number the merchant asks for at handoff. The phone lives at the account
level (the OTP anchor); assignability (`is_active`) matters to the
rider's own screen too.

products.description:
Empty `q`: the most-purchased products (real order counts). With
`q`: catalog-name matches, alphabetical. Availability and the
open-store rule are enforced server-side either way.

stores.description:
Empty `q`: all open stores. With `q`: name/category matches —
nearest first when the request carries a location.

StoreOrderResponse.description:
A store order as the customer sees it: one store's slice of the
checkout, with its own status and totals.

StoreProductResponse.description:
A store_product as the merchant sees it: its catalog identity, its
store, and its sell configuration.

stock.description:
`null` = untracked (made to order). A number is reserved atomically
at checkout.

StoreResponse.description: A store as the API returns it. Integer RWF for money, ISO-8601 times.

distance_m.description:
Straight-line meters from the customer, when the request carried
`lat`/`lng` and the store has coordinates. Server-computed — the
client never does geo math.

eta_min.description:
Pure ride time at Kigali's effective moto speed (`~` prefix in the
UI). Present exactly when `distance_m` is.

changed_at.description: Echo this back as `since` on the next poll.

UpdateCustomerInput.description:
Admin edits to a customer account. Provided fields overwrite, an empty
name clears it, absent fields keep their value. Phone stays editable
because a typo'd number during OTP signup is exactly the kind of thing
an admin corrects; a taken phone is the typed 409.

UpdateMerchantInput.description:
Admin edits to a business. Every field is optional: provided fields
overwrite, an empty string clears an optional contact field, absent
fields keep their value. Suspension is the pause tool — a suspended
business is refused by the merchant wing and stops taking orders.

UpdateRiderInput.description:
Admin edits to a rider. Provided fields overwrite, absent fields keep
their value. A phone edit changes the OTP anchor (the account) and the
rider's display phone together; a taken phone is the typed 409. An
empty name is a 400 — rider names are NOT NULL, there is nothing to
clear to.

UpdateStoreProductInput.description:
PATCH on the sell configuration: price, stock (a number sets it, explicit
`null` switches back to untracked), availability, SKU. Absent fields
keep their value.

stock.description: Absent = keep, `null` = untracked, a number = the on-hand count.
